FACTULAL POSITION AND PLEADINGS 2.

The brief facts relevant for disposal of the present DAR are that on 21.11.2022 injured alongwith his wife were coming to their home from Sector 22, Rohini on scooty bearing registration no.
DL 8S CQ 7359.

At around 12:45 pm, when they reached near New MCD School Pratap Vihar, Delhi, one tractor bearing registration no. HR 12U 8406 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle)
attached with a tanker came from front side, which was being driven by its driver/R1 in high speed, rashly and negligently and hit the scooty of the injured due to which injured sustained injuries on his right foot.
R1 alongwith offending vehicle fled away from the spot.
Injured was taken to Shree Aggarsain International Hospital and remained admitted there till 23.11.2023.
FIR no. 1078/22 was registered at PS Aman Vihar for the offences punishable under Section 279/337 IPC.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by MACT Case No. 209/2023 (FIR no. 1078/22)

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. sentences.text: In order to prove this issue, the petitioner has examined himself as Pw1 in this case.
Petitioner has brought on record his medical record i.e. Ex.Pw1/3 & Ex.Pw1/4 and also proved DAR.
It is claim of R1 that injured had hit the offending vehicle from behind.
However, R1 has not examined himself or any other witness to prove this fact.
It is claimed by R2 that offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the present case as registration number of the offending vehicle is not mentioned in the FIR.

Record shows that wife of injured, who was with the injured at the time of accident,
informed the police vide GD no. 97A dated 22.11.2022 about the registration number of the offending vehicle and his location at that time after which the offending vehicle was seized on the same day.

Moreover, there is affidavit of R1, filed alongwith DAR, admitting that on the date of accident, he was driving the MACT Case No. 209/2023 (FIR no. 1078/22) Rakesh Thakur Vs.
Sukhbir Singh Page no. 6 of 15 VIKRAM 2025.12.22 offending vehicle which met with an accident near Nithari School Delhi.
Therefore, claim of R2 that offending vehicle has been falsely implicated in the present case is of no consequence.
R1 has not filed any complaint with respect to his false implication in the present case.

Keeping in view the facts & evidence produced by the petitioner, it has proved on record that the said accident has taken place with the offending vehicle being driven by respondent no.1, as a result of which, the petitioner sustained injuries.

12. In view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the rashness and negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle, which is clearly visible and as such, was responsible not only for this accident, but also for everything that followed thereafter.
Accordingly issue no.1 is decided in favour of the petitioner and against the respondents.

13. As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
14. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.

In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. pecuniary as well as non- MACT Case No. 209/2023 (FIR no. 1078/22) Rakesh Thakur Vs. Sukhbir Singh Page no. 7 of 15 Digitally signed by VIKRAM VIKRAM Date:
2025.12.22 16:14:03 +0530 pecuniary damages.

The pecuniary damages or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The non- pecuniary or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment,
special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage Rakesh Thakur vs Sukhbir Singh on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94705634/
5 prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in MACT Case No. 209/2023 (FIR no. 1078/22) Rakesh Thakur Vs. Sukhbir Singh Page no. 8 of 15 VIKRAM Date:
calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited, (2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.

As per medical documents, injured MACT Case No. 209/2023 (FIR no. 1078/22) Rakesh Thakur Vs.

As per discharge summary, injured was diagnosed with 'Fracture medial malleolus with deltoid ligament injury with dislocation of inferior tibiofibular joint right with fracture lower 1/3rd fibula right with haemarthrosis right ankle with soft tissue contusion'.

He would have taken special rich protein/calcium diet for his speedy recovery and would have been definitely helped by some person Rakesh Thakur vs Sukhbir Singh on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94705634/

for special diet, Rs. 30,000/- towards attendant and Rs. 30,000/- for conveyance charges to the petitioner.
Hence, an amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- be awarded as attendant and special diet head.
Pain and Suffering 18.

As per the medical documents, injured suffered grievous injuries (Fracture medial malleolus with deltoid ligament injury with dislocation of inferior tibiofibular joint right with fracture lower 1/3rd fibula right with haemarthrosis right ankle with soft tissue contusion) in the road traffic accident on 21.11.2022.
Injured was remained admitted from 21.11.2022 to 23.11.2023 and thereafter, he remained under treatment till September, 2023.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to injured for the shock, pain MACT Case No. 209/2023 (FIR no.
1078/22) Rakesh Thakur Vs. Sukhbir Singh Page no. 10 of 15

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by injured and duration of the treatment etc., an amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- is being awarded to his towards pain and sufferings during the said period of his treatment and immobility.

Thus, he is awarded a total amount of Rs. 1,00,000/-
under this head.
Loss of Actual Earnings 19.
Injured deposed that he was UDC, posted in Govt. Boys Senior Secondary School, Nithari on the day of accident and was getting a salary of Rs. 55,293/-.

It cannot be overlooked that petitioner has availed Medical/Earned leave of total 05 months and 21 days days.

LIABILITY 23.
In the case in hand, offending vehicle was insured with R2.
However, it is claimed by R2 that there is breach of insurance policy as the offending vehicle was attached with a tanker for which permit and commercial driving licence is required.
The DAR shows that the accident was caused with the front of tractor and not with the tanker.
As the tractor's negligence was the root cause, even if the tanker lacked separate insurance, R2 cannot be absolved from his liability to compensate the injured.

See: The Royal Sundram Allilance Insurance Company Limited Vs. Honnamma & Ors.,
2025 INS 625.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by MACT Case No. 209/2023 (FIR no. 1078/22)

strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
& Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

14. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. pecuniary as well as non- MACT Case No. 209/2023 (FIR no. 1078/22) Rakesh Thakur Vs. Sukhbir Singh Page no. 7 of 15 Digitally signed by VIKRAM VIKRAM Date:
2025.12.22 16:14:03 +0530 pecuniary damages.
The pecuniary damages or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The non- pecuniary or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment,
special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc. and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage Rakesh Thakur vs Sukhbir Singh on 22 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94705634/
5 prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.
It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in MACT Case No. 209/2023 (FIR no. 1078/22) Rakesh Thakur Vs. Sukhbir Singh Page no. 8 of 15 VIKRAM Date:
